summary: As of October 15, 2026, junk-bond spreads are 3.23 percentage points, +0.08 percentage points over five trading days, and the junk-versus-safe gap is 2.39 percentage points. VIX is 16.46 and the 3-month VIX is 18.49, so near-term fear is below the 3-month reading. The Nasdaq-100 is -4.2 percent from its trailing high, semiconductors are +9.5 percent versus their 200-day average, and 73 percent of the 30-name list is above its own 200-day average.
what_would_change_this: The headline would leave risk-on if junk spreads reached 4.50 percentage points, near-term volatility rose above the 3-month reading by more than half a point, or the Nasdaq-100 fell more than 10 percent below its trailing high.
what_the_tape_is_saying: As of October 15, 2026, junk-bond spreads are 3.23 percentage points and are up 0.08 percentage points over five trading days. Investment-grade spreads are up 0.02 percentage points over those same five trading days. The CCC-minus-BB gap is 10.81 percentage points. Of the 0.03 percentage-point move in the all-in junk yield, 0.08 was the credit spread and 0.11 was Treasury rates. The 10-year yield is 5.10 percent as of October 15, 2026 and the 30-year is 5.43 percent as of October 15, 2026, a gap of 0.33 percentage points. Brent is 109.69 dollars a barrel as of October 16, 2026 (+4.75 percent over five trading days), and the curve is backwardation. The 5-year inflation breakeven is 2.37 percent as of October 16, 2026, unchanged over five observations. The 10-year real yield is 2.78 percent as of October 15, 2026. The broad dollar index is 121.60 as of October 9, 2026, +3.39 index points over 20 observations. VIX is 16.46 as of October 15, 2026. The Fed balance sheet is 6.76 trillion dollars as of October 14, 2026, up 9 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Reserve balances are 3.02 trillion dollars as of October 14, 2026, up 8 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations.
